title: Metabolism of Lipids
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 300L Metabolism of Lipids curriculum: lipid classification and fatty acid nomenclature, digestion/absorption, beta-oxidation and ketogenesis, fatty acid and triacylglycerol biosynthesis, cholesterol synthesis and regulation, lipoprotein transport, phospholipid metabolism, eicosanoids, and essential fatty acids/lipid disorders. Content is kept to the lipid class only, distinct from carbohydrate/protein/nucleic-acid metabolism courses.

questions.question: In fatty acid nomenclature, the notation 18:2(n-6) (linoleic acid) indicates a fatty acid with:
options: 18 carbons, 2 double bonds, first double bond 6 carbons from the carboxyl end
18 carbons, 2 double bonds, first double bond 6 carbons from the methyl (omega) end
2 carbons, 18 double bonds from the carboxyl end
questions.correct_answer: 18 carbons, 2 double bonds, first double bond 6 carbons from the methyl (omega) end
questions.explanation: The format is (carbon number):(number of double bonds)(n-x), where n-x counts from the methyl (omega) end; 18:2(n-6) means an 18-carbon chain with 2 double bonds, the first located at carbon 6 from the omega end.

questions.question: Which of the following is classified as an essential fatty acid that must be obtained from the diet because humans lack the enzymes to synthesize it?
questions.explanation: Humans lack desaturase enzymes able to introduce double bonds beyond carbon 9 (counting from the carboxyl end), so linoleic acid (18:2, n-6) and alpha-linolenic acid (18:3, n-3) cannot be synthesized de novo and are dietary essentials.

questions.question: Dietary triacylglycerols are digested in the small intestine primarily by which enzyme?
questions.explanation: Pancreatic lipase, acting with colipase at the oil-water interface of bile-salt-emulsified fat droplets, hydrolyzes dietary triacylglycerols mainly to 2-monoacylglycerol and free fatty acids.

questions.question: Bile salts aid fat digestion mainly by:
options: Directly hydrolyzing ester bonds in triacylglycerols
Emulsifying dietary fat into small micelles/droplets, increasing surface area for lipase action
Inhibiting pancreatic lipase to slow digestion
questions.correct_answer: Emulsifying dietary fat into small micelles/droplets, increasing surface area for lipase action
questions.explanation: Bile salts are amphipathic molecules that emulsify large fat globules into smaller droplets and form mixed micelles, greatly increasing the surface area accessible to pancreatic lipase and aiding absorption of digestion products.

questions.question: After absorption by intestinal mucosal cells, resynthesized triacylglycerols are packaged with proteins into which lipoprotein particle for transport via the lymphatics?
questions.explanation: Enterocytes resynthesize triacylglycerols from absorbed monoacylglycerol and fatty acids and package them, with apolipoprotein B-48 and cholesterol, into chylomicrons, which enter the lymphatic lacteals before reaching the bloodstream.

questions.question: Before a long-chain fatty acid can be beta-oxidized in the mitochondrial matrix, it must first be activated in the cytosol to form:
questions.explanation: Fatty acid activation, catalyzed by acyl-CoA synthetase (thiokinase) using ATP and coenzyme A, converts a free fatty acid into fatty acyl-CoA, the form required for entry into beta-oxidation.

questions.question: Long-chain fatty acyl-CoA is transported into the mitochondrial matrix for beta-oxidation via the:
questions.explanation: Because the inner mitochondrial membrane is impermeable to long-chain acyl-CoA, carnitine palmitoyltransferase I (CPT I) converts it to acylcarnitine, which crosses via a translocase, and CPT II regenerates acyl-CoA in the matrix.

questions.question: Each cycle of beta-oxidation of a fatty acid removes how many carbons, in the form of acetyl-CoA, from the acyl chain?
questions.explanation: Each round of the four-step beta-oxidation spiral (oxidation, hydration, oxidation, thiolytic cleavage) shortens the fatty acyl chain by two carbons, released as one molecule of acetyl-CoA.

questions.question: In the beta-oxidation spiral, the enzyme acyl-CoA dehydrogenase catalyzes the first oxidative step, transferring electrons directly to:
questions.explanation: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenase introduces a trans double bond between C2-C3 while reducing its FAD prosthetic group; the electrons are then passed to electron-transferring flavoprotein (ETF) and into the electron transport chain.

questions.question: Complete beta-oxidation of palmitic acid (C16) yields how many molecules of acetyl-CoA?
questions.explanation: A 16-carbon fatty acid undergoes 7 rounds of beta-oxidation, cleaving the chain into 8 two-carbon acetyl-CoA units.

questions.question: Ketone bodies (acetoacetate, beta-hydroxybutyrate, acetone) are synthesized primarily in the:
questions.explanation: Ketogenesis occurs in hepatic mitochondria, especially during prolonged fasting or uncontrolled diabetes, when excess acetyl-CoA from fatty acid oxidation exceeds the capacity of the TCA cycle (limited oxaloacetate).

questions.question: The rate-limiting/regulatory enzyme of ketogenesis, which condenses acetoacetyl-CoA and acetyl-CoA to form HMG-CoA, is:
questions.explanation: Mitochondrial HMG-CoA synthase catalyzes the key regulatory step of ketogenesis, forming HMG-CoA, which HMG-CoA lyase then cleaves to acetoacetate and acetyl-CoA.

questions.question: Why can the liver produce ketone bodies for other tissues but cannot itself use them for energy?
options: The liver lacks succinyl-CoA:3-ketoacid CoA transferase (thiophorase), needed to reactivate acetoacetate to acetoacetyl-CoA
Ketone bodies are toxic to hepatocytes
The liver cannot transport ketone bodies out of the cell
questions.correct_answer: The liver lacks succinyl-CoA:3-ketoacid CoA transferase (thiophorase), needed to reactivate acetoacetate to acetoacetyl-CoA
questions.explanation: Extrahepatic tissues (muscle, brain) use thiophorase to convert acetoacetate back to acetoacetyl-CoA for entry into the TCA cycle; hepatocytes lack this enzyme, so the liver exports ketone bodies rather than oxidizing them.

questions.question: The rate-limiting enzyme of de novo fatty acid synthesis, which carboxylates acetyl-CoA to malonyl-CoA, is:
questions.explanation: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC), a biotin-dependent enzyme, catalyzes the committed, rate-limiting step of fatty acid synthesis: carboxylation of acetyl-CoA to malonyl-CoA, using ATP and CO2/bicarbonate.

questions.question: Fatty acid synthase uses which reduced coenzyme as the source of reducing power for chain elongation?
questions.explanation: Unlike beta-oxidation, which produces NADH and FADH2, fatty acid synthesis is reductive and consumes NADPH (largely supplied by the pentose phosphate pathway and the malic enzyme reaction) at both reduction steps of each elongation cycle.

questions.question: Citrate serves a key role in cytosolic fatty acid synthesis by:
options: Directly acting as the carbon donor for chain elongation
Being transported from mitochondria to cytosol, where ATP-citrate lyase cleaves it to yield acetyl-CoA and oxaloacetate
Serving as the coenzyme for acetyl-CoA carboxylase
questions.correct_answer: Being transported from mitochondria to cytosol, where ATP-citrate lyase cleaves it to yield acetyl-CoA and oxaloacetate
questions.explanation: Mitochondrial acetyl-CoA (from pyruvate or fatty acid oxidation) cannot cross the inner mitochondrial membrane directly, so it condenses with oxaloacetate to citrate, which is exported and cleaved by ATP-citrate lyase in the cytosol to regenerate acetyl-CoA for fatty acid synthesis.

questions.question: Malonyl-CoA, in addition to being a fatty acid synthesis intermediate, also regulates beta-oxidation by:
options: Allosterically inhibiting carnitine palmitoyltransferase I (CPT I), preventing simultaneous synthesis and oxidation of fatty acids
questions.correct_answer: Allosterically inhibiting carnitine palmitoyltransferase I (CPT I), preventing simultaneous synthesis and oxidation of fatty acids
questions.explanation: Malonyl-CoA inhibits CPT I on the outer mitochondrial membrane, blocking fatty acid entry into mitochondria for oxidation whenever fatty acid synthesis is active, avoiding a futile cycle.

questions.question: The final step of triacylglycerol synthesis involves the addition of a fatty acyl group to which intermediate?
questions.explanation: Triacylglycerol synthesis proceeds via glycerol-3-phosphate to phosphatidic acid, which is dephosphorylated to 1,2-diacylglycerol; diacylglycerol acyltransferase then adds a third fatty acyl group to form triacylglycerol.

questions.question: Hormone-sensitive lipase in adipose tissue, which mobilizes stored fat by hydrolyzing triacylglycerols, is activated by:
options: Glucagon and epinephrine, via cAMP-dependent protein kinase A phosphorylation
questions.correct_answer: Glucagon and epinephrine, via cAMP-dependent protein kinase A phosphorylation
questions.explanation: During fasting or stress, glucagon/epinephrine raise cAMP and activate PKA, which phosphorylates and activates hormone-sensitive lipase (and perilipin), promoting lipolysis of stored triacylglycerol; insulin has the opposite, inhibitory effect.

questions.question: VLDL particles, synthesized in the liver, function mainly to:
options: Transport dietary lipids from the intestine
Transport endogenously synthesized triacylglycerols from the liver to peripheral tissues
Return excess cholesterol from peripheral tissues to the liver
Digest dietary fat in the intestinal lumen
questions.correct_answer: Transport endogenously synthesized triacylglycerols from the liver to peripheral tissues
questions.explanation: VLDL (very-low-density lipoprotein), assembled in hepatocytes with apoB-100, carries newly synthesized triacylglycerol and cholesterol from the liver to peripheral tissues, where lipoprotein lipase releases fatty acids.

questions.question: As VLDL loses triacylglycerol via the action of lipoprotein lipase in capillary beds, it is progressively converted to intermediate-density lipoprotein and finally to:
questions.explanation: As VLDL is progressively depleted of triacylglycerol by lipoprotein lipase, it becomes IDL and then LDL, a cholesterol-ester-rich particle that delivers cholesterol to peripheral tissues via LDL receptor-mediated endocytosis.

questions.question: HDL particles contribute to reverse cholesterol transport largely through the action of which enzyme, which esterifies free cholesterol on the HDL surface?
questions.explanation: LCAT, activated by apoA-I on nascent HDL, transfers a fatty acyl group from lecithin (phosphatidylcholine) to free cholesterol, forming cholesteryl esters that are sequestered in the HDL core, driving reverse cholesterol transport to the liver.

questions.question: The rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol biosynthesis, the major site of statin drug action, is:
questions.explanation: HMG-CoA reductase catalyzes the committed, rate-limiting step of cholesterol synthesis (reduction of HMG-CoA to mevalonate) and is the target of statin drugs, which competitively inhibit it to lower plasma cholesterol.

questions.question: Cellular cholesterol levels feedback-regulate HMG-CoA reductase mainly by:
options: Increasing transcription of the HMG-CoA reductase gene as cholesterol rises
Suppressing SREBP-mediated transcription and promoting degradation of HMG-CoA reductase as cholesterol accumulates
Having no effect on the enzyme
questions.correct_answer: Suppressing SREBP-mediated transcription and promoting degradation of HMG-CoA reductase as cholesterol accumulates
questions.explanation: Rising intracellular cholesterol inhibits proteolytic activation of SREBP-2 (reducing transcription of HMG-CoA reductase and the LDL receptor) and accelerates HMG-CoA reductase degradation, providing tight feedback control of cholesterol synthesis.

questions.question: Cholesterol serves as the metabolic precursor for all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Cholesterol is the precursor of bile acids, steroid hormones (glucocorticoids, mineralocorticoids, sex hormones), and vitamin D; heme, by contrast, is synthesized from glycine and succinyl-CoA, not from cholesterol.

questions.question: In phospholipid (phosphatidylcholine) biosynthesis via the CDP-choline (Kennedy) pathway, choline must first be activated by combining with:
options: ATP to form phosphocholine, then CTP to form CDP-choline
questions.correct_answer: ATP to form phosphocholine, then CTP to form CDP-choline
questions.explanation: In the Kennedy pathway, choline kinase phosphorylates choline using ATP to form phosphocholine, which is then activated by CTP (via CTP:phosphocholine cytidylyltransferase) to CDP-choline before transfer onto diacylglycerol.

questions.question: Phospholipase A2 catalyzes the hydrolysis of membrane phospholipids to release which important eicosanoid precursor?
questions.explanation: Phospholipase A2 cleaves the sn-2 ester bond of membrane phospholipids, liberating arachidonic acid, the principal 20-carbon polyunsaturated fatty acid substrate for prostaglandin, thromboxane, and leukotriene synthesis.

questions.question: Cyclooxygenase (COX) converts arachidonic acid into which class of eicosanoids?
questions.explanation: COX (prostaglandin H synthase) oxidizes and cyclizes arachidonic acid to prostaglandin H2, the common precursor of prostaglandins and thromboxanes, while the lipoxygenase pathway produces leukotrienes.

questions.question: Thromboxane A2, produced mainly by platelets, has which principal physiological effect?
options: Vasodilation and inhibition of platelet aggregation
Vasoconstriction and promotion of platelet aggregation
questions.correct_answer: Vasoconstriction and promotion of platelet aggregation
questions.explanation: Thromboxane A2 promotes platelet aggregation and vasoconstriction, contributing to blood clot formation, in contrast to prostacyclin (PGI2) from vascular endothelium, which has opposing vasodilatory, anti-aggregatory effects.

questions.question: A patient presenting with recurrent episodes of severe abdominal pain, eruptive skin xanthomas, and grossly elevated fasting plasma chylomicrons is most consistent with a deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Familial lipoprotein lipase deficiency (or apoC-II deficiency, its activator) impairs clearance of chylomicrons and VLDL triacylglycerol, causing severe hypertriglyceridemia (type I hyperlipoproteinemia) with abdominal pain, eruptive xanthomas, and lipemic plasma.

questions.question: Familial hypercholesterolemia, a common inherited dyslipidemia causing premature atherosclerosis, most often results from mutations affecting:
questions.explanation: Familial hypercholesterolemia is classically caused by mutations in the LDL receptor gene, impairing hepatic clearance of LDL from plasma and leading to markedly elevated LDL cholesterol and early atherosclerosis.

questions.question: Sphingolipids, structural components of cell membranes and myelin, are built on a backbone of:
questions.explanation: Unlike glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids (sphingomyelin, cerebrosides, gangliosides) are built on the amino-alcohol backbone sphingosine rather than glycerol.

questions.question: In beta-oxidation of odd-chain fatty acids, the final propionyl-CoA product is converted, via methylmalonyl-CoA, into succinyl-CoA by a reaction that requires which vitamin-derived coenzyme?
options: Biotin only, with no B12 requirement
questions.explanation: Propionyl-CoA is carboxylated (biotin-dependent) to methylmalonyl-CoA, which methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, a vitamin B12 (adenosylcobalamin)-dependent enzyme, isomerizes to succinyl-CoA for entry into the TCA cycle.

questions.question: Compared with saturated fatty acid oxidation, beta-oxidation of an unsaturated fatty acid such as oleic acid requires an additional enzyme, isomerase, mainly because:
options: Unsaturated fatty acids cannot be activated to acyl-CoA
The naturally occurring cis double bond must be repositioned/converted to the trans configuration recognized by the normal beta-oxidation enzymes
Unsaturated fatty acids are not transported by carnitine
Unsaturated fatty acids yield propionyl-CoA instead of acetyl-CoA
questions.correct_answer: The naturally occurring cis double bond must be repositioned/converted to the trans configuration recognized by the normal beta-oxidation enzymes
questions.explanation: When beta-oxidation reaches a cis double bond at an odd-numbered carbon, enoyl-CoA isomerase repositions/converts it to the trans-Δ2 configuration so that the standard hydratase can act, allowing oxidation to continue.
